mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate component of equity discount rates, increasing present values of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 4.0% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of observations (p > 0.05 for t-test against zero returns) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% in more than 40% of observations over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises (FEDFUNDS increase) and unemployment is below 4.0% (UNRATE < 4.0%), the market perceives unsustainable tightening that threatens growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS rise + UNRATE < 4.0%) fails to generate negative returns in more than 40% of instances (p > 0.05 for t-test against zero returns) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), a declining unemployment rate signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost corporate hiring and earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0%, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in more than 40% of observations over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS increase) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of observations (p > 0.05 for t-test against zero returns) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1800 thousand units (HOUST > 1800) signal strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, boosting economic growth and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when HOUST exceeds 1800 in more than 40% of observations over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise and industrial production (INDPRO) expands (INDPRO > 110), the combined signal indicates synchronized demand and supply chain strength that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (HOUST rise + INDPRO > 110) fails to generate positive returns in more than 40% of instances (p > 0.05 for t-test against zero returns) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In strong GDP expansion regimes (GDPC1 > 11400 billion dollars), sustained real economic growth signals elevated corporate profitability that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 exceeds 11400, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in more than 40% of observations over any 3-year rolling window.
